transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is an electrical fault where the washing machine is causing your RCD (the switch that trips to protect against electric shock) to cut power. Because this involves a risk of electric shock, please do not keep resetting the fuse box and running the machine; it needs to be checked by a qualified engineer before further use. The most common cause for an Indesit washing machine tripping the electricity intermittently is the heater element developing a leak to earth (a short circuit). This usually happens only when the cycle reaches the heating stage. Other possibilities include a fault in the drain pump, the motor, or damaged wiring/plug. To help identify which component is likely at fault, could you tell me: does the power trip happen immediately when you switch the machine on (before it starts filling), or only after it has been running for a few minutes and started heating the water?

It's not straight away. It trips a few minutes into the 40 or 60 degree washes, and it has never tripped on cold, quick 30 or rinse and spin. I have been resetting it each time, as it has done it a few times this past month. There's been no burning smell and I haven't seen any sparking.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The fact that it only trips on the heated cycles (40°C or 60°C) and never on cold ones suggests this is an earth fault in a component used during heating. The most common cause for Indesit machines like yours is the heater element developing a leak to the metal casing, which sends current into the ground and trips your RCD. Because this involves live mains voltage and a risk of electric shock, you must not keep resetting the fuse box or attempting to use the machine. It needs to be isolated from the power supply immediately. Please arrange for a qualified appliance engineer to inspect it. They will need to test the heater element (and potentially the pump or wiring) with appropriate safety equipment. Do not attempt to open the machine or test components yourself unless you are fully trained and comfortable working with mains electricity.

candidates: Mains wiring, plug or internal harness short (low)
